=== COLUMN 2 ===
The Old, The Very Old, The Very New
WALT CHERNOKAL PHOTO
Jimmy Clark, Duns, Scotland, in his sleek, low slung Lotus-Ford #92, brand new for the 1963 summer
racing season was lapping #21-John Pfrommer Sp. driven by Johnny White, Warren, Mich. and #7-Len Sutton,
Portland, Ore., the Leader Card Spl. White's mount was at least eight years old, Sutton's two years old. Neither
car stood a chance of beating Clark's speedy little mount. White tried hard but his mount just got tired and quit.
Sutton eased up and did finish the race. It was the 200 miler here last August.
HOT SCOT AND FRIEND
Jimmy Clark of Duns, Scotland
and his #92 Lotus-Ford will never be
forgotten by Milwaukee racing fans.
A truly great combination that hum-
bled one of the finest fields of cars and
drivers ever assembled.
Clark went on to win the world's
driving championship with one of the
most fearsome displays of speed and
handling ever seen here in America
or for that matter, anyplace else. The
field of drivers had no reason to be
LOTUSFord
ashamed in defeat. The 255 cubic inch
Ford engine built with a general Fair-
lane block employed all the latest
techniques to make the engine light-
weight, durable, and efficient.
The handling qualities of the car were truly remarkable. It didn't bounce over the little depressions in the
race track. It seemed to crawl over each low spot like a spider. It took builder Colin Chapman 13 years to get
his point across and he did it with absolute devastation at Milwaukee.
